# Adjudication Task — Chapter 52

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃52화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|오전 여섯 시.
  6|
  7|택시 기사 김 씨는 오늘의 첫 손님을 태웠다. 그리고 10분 만에 후회했다.
  8|
  9|‘재수 옴 붙었네.’
 10|
 11|겉보기로는 멀쩡하게 생긴 청년이다. 근육질의 듬직한 덩치에 얼굴은 멀끔해서 많이 쳐 줘야 20대 중후반으로 보였다.
 12|
 13|그런데…….
 14|
 15|“킁카킁카.”
 16|
 17|이상하다. 좀 많이.
 18|
 19|“흐어어.”
 20|
 21|웬 드링크 박스를 보물처럼 꼭 껴안고, 30초에 한 번씩 슬쩍 열어 냄새를 맡는다. 그리고 뭐에 홀린 것처럼 몸을 부르르 떤다.
 22|
 23|‘시방 저게 뭐 하는 짓이여.’
 24|
 25|김 씨는 뒷골이 싸했다. 10년 넘게 택시를 몰았지만 이런 종류의 진상은 처음이다.
 26|
 27|그가 계속해서 옆자리 청년을 곁눈질하던 그 순간.
 28|
 29|“아저씨.”
 30|
 31|“예, 예?!”
 32|
 33|심장 떨어질 뻔했다.
 34|
 35|방금 전까지만 해도 퀭하던 청년의 눈동자가, 야수처럼 번뜩이고 있었다.
 36|
 37|“뒤에 트럭이요.”
 38|
 39|“트, 트럭이요? 파란색?”
 40|
 41|“네. 아까 사거리에서부터 따라오는 것 같지 않아요?”
 42|
 43|“예? 아니 뭐, 그렇긴 한 것 같은데.”
 44|
 45|“미행일지도 모르잖아요.”
 46|
 47|이건 또 무슨 참신한 개소린가.
 48|
 49|김 씨는 눈동자를 뒤룩뒤룩 굴리다가 결국 그가 원하는 듯해 보이는 원하는 대답을 내놨다.
 50|
 51|“여, 옆쪽으로 빠지겠습니다.”
 52|
 53|청년은 파란 트럭이 시야에서 사라질 때까지 드링크 박스를 꼭 껴안고 있었다. 마치 누군가가 뺏어 가기라도 할 것처럼.
 54|
 55|“습하. 습하.”
 56|
 57|물론 틈틈이 냄새를 맡는 것도 빼놓지 않았다.
 58|
 59|‘이건 제대로 미친놈이다.’
 60|
 61|차 내부는 에어컨 바람이 쌩쌩 부는데, 김 씨의 등허리는 식은땀으로 축축했다. 첫 개시부터 이 모양이라니.
 62|
 63|아주 재수 옴 붙은 날이다.
 64|
 65|
 66|
 67|* * *
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|부아앙.
 72|
 73|요금을 건네고 문을 닫자마자 택시가 총알처럼 튀어 나간다.
 74|
 75|누가 보면 뒤에서 몬스터라도 쫓아오는 줄 알겠네. 사고라도 나면 어쩌려고. 나는 쯧쯧 혀를 차고 아파트 단지로 들어섰다.
 76|
 77|품에는 어제 받은 드링크 박스를 소중히 껴안은 채였다.
 78|
 79|‘3억.’
 80|
 81|내가 F급 헌터 시절부터 꼬박 3년을 일해서 모은 돈이랑 비슷한 액수다. 물론 지금은 한 푼도 안 남았다.
 82|
 83|‘빚 갚는 데 다 썼지.’
 84|
 85|그렇게 빚에 허덕이던 때가 있었는데, 이 악물고 하다 보니 점점 나아졌다. 가족을 일산 근처의 안전지대 아파트로 이사 보내기도 했고. 근래 들어서는 뭐, 인생이 롤러코스터 같다.
 86|
 87|시스템이 사라지면 추락하는 롤러코스터…….
 88|
 89|아니다. 몇 달 만에 오는 집인데 이런 생각은 집어치우자.
 90|
 91|‘그런데 몇 동 몇 호였지?’
 92|
 93|두어 달에 한 번 꼴로 오는 집이다 보니 늘 이렇다.
 94|
 95|나는 다닥다닥 붙어 있는 아파트 단지를 노려보다가 핸드폰을 꺼내 전화를 걸었다. 한참 신호음이 울린 뒤에야 연결됐다.
 96|
 97|딸칵.
 98|
 99|- 여보세요?
100|
101|아직 이른 시각이라 자고 있을 줄 알았는데, 하연이의 목소리는 또렷했다.
102|
103|“일어나 있었어?”
104|
105|- 일어나 있어야지. 시간이 몇 신데.
106|
107|“아직 일곱 시도 안 됐는데.”
108|
109|- 일찍 일어나야 공부가 잘돼.
110|
111|내 동생이지만 감탄스럽다. 오전 기상을 7대 죄악쯤으로 여기는 진호 형이 이걸 들었어야 했는데.
112|
113|- 왜 전화했어?
114|
115|“내가 지금 집 앞이거든.”
116|
117|- 응? 집 앞이라고?
118|
119|“어. 근데 우리 집이 어딘지 까먹었어.”
120|
121|- ……또? 가지가지 한다, 진짜. 기다려.
122|
123|끊긴 전화를 붙잡고 몇 분쯤 기다렸을까, 어느 동 입구에서 여자애 하나가 슬리퍼를 질질 끌며 나타났다.
124|
125|멀리서도 느껴지는 날백수 포스. 세상 귀찮다는 그 표정을 보자 나도 모르게 웃음이 나왔다.
126|
127|“진하연!”
128|
129|“소리 지르지 마. 사람들 깨.”
130|
131|……그래, 이래야 내 동생이지.
132|
133|“웬일이야? 말도 없이.”
134|
135|“내가 우리 집 오는데 말하고 와야 되냐?”
136|
137|“하도 드문드문 오니까 그렇지. 부녀회장이 오빠보다 우리 집 더 자주 올걸?”
138|
139|“그 정도냐?”
140|
141|“그 정도지.”
142|
143|그때 엘리베이터가 멈췄다. 현관문 앞에 선 하연이가 비밀번호를 입력하고 문고리를 돌린다.
144|
145|그리고 그곳에…….
146|
147|“아들!”
148|
149|환하게 웃고 있는 한 사람이 있다. 주름진 손과 반쯤 풀린 파마머리. 깜짝 선물을 받은 어린아이처럼 좋아하는 그 모습.
150|
151|순간 목이 막힌 나는 턱을 긁적이다가 풀썩 웃어 버렸다.
152|
153|“저 왔어요, 엄마.”
154|
155|드디어 돌아왔다.
156|
157|가족이 기다리고 있는 그곳. 집으로.
158|
159|
160|
161|* * *
162|
163|
164|
165|지글지글.
166|
167|엄마는 부엌에서 아침 준비로 한창이다. 기분 좋은 냄새가 코끝을 맴돌았다.
168|
169|“오랜만에 아들 왔다고 아주 신나셨네, 우리 김 여사.”
170|
171|하연이가 배를 벅벅 긁으며 옆자리에 주저앉았다.
172|
173|낡은 소파가 푹 꺼진다. 돼지 같은 년.
174|
175|“요리 많이 준비하고 계셔?”
176|
177|“어. 완전 진수성찬. 덕분에 잘 먹겠네.”
178|
179|대답은 하는데, 눈은 핸드폰 화면에 박혀 있다.
180|
181|“넌 오랜만에 오빠 봤는데 반갑지도 않냐?”
182|
183|“응?”
184|
185|“아니, 뭐. 고생했다고 어깨라도 좀 주물러 줄 수도 있고.”
186|
187|하연이가 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
188|
189|“왜 이래, 태경 씨. 우리 그런 사이 아니잖아.”
190|
191|“……말하는 싸가지 봐라.”
192|
193|이렇게 티격태격 하는 게 하루 이틀은 아니지만 괜히 섭섭하다.
194|
195|나는, 어? 그렇게 죽을 고비 넘겨 가면서 겨우 돌아왔는데!
196|
197|“지금 울컥했다. 울컥했지?”
198|
199|눈치 하나는 귀신이다.
200|
201|“학교 갈 준비나 해. 급식충아.”
202|
203|“응. 오늘 개교기념일.”
204|
205|주먹이 파르르 떨린다. 당장이라도 저 얄미운 뒤통수를 후려치고 싶지만 그러면 진짜 지는 거다.
206|
207|“때리고 싶죠? 주먹 부들부들 하죠?”
208|
209|“넌 여자라서 살았다. 불알만 달려 있었어도…….”
210|
211|“엄마! 오빠가 나 성추행해!”
212|
213|“야, 야!”
214|
215|“오빠가 나한테 불. 읍, 읍!”
216|
217|입을 틀어 막힌 하연이가 발버둥 친다. 때리고, 꼬집고. 그래 봤자 열아홉 살 여자애라 아프지도 않다.
218|
219|그러다가 우연히, 녀석이 내뻗은 발이 소파 한구석에 고이 모셔 둔 드링크 박스를 강타했다.
220|
221|퍽.
222|
223|촤르르륵.
224|
225|활짝 열린 박스. 거실 바닥에 쏟아지는 누런 지폐 뭉치.
226|
227|순간, 하연이의 몸이 굳었다.
228|
229|“이제 그만들 싸우고 아침 먹……어.”
230|
231|거기에 부엌에서 나온 엄마까지.
232|
233|일시 정지 버튼을 누른 것처럼 모든 게 멈춘 거실에, 찌개 끓는 소리만 잔잔하게 깔렸다.
234|
235|지글지글.
236|
237|나는 어색하게 웃으며 입을 열었다.
238|
239|“밥 먹고 말하면 안 될까요?”
240|
241|“……아들?”
242|
243|“읍읍읍.”
244|
245|아무래도 아침 식사는 한참 뒤로 미뤄질 것 같다.
246|
247|
248|
249|* * *
250|
251|
252|
253|가족들에게 지금까지의 일들을 적당히 각색해서 들려 주었다.
254|
255|C급으로의 재각성, 그리고 돈의 출처까지.
256|
257|“그렇게 된 거예요.”
258|
259|반응은 두 가지로 나뉘었다.
260|
261|“그렇구나.”
262|
263|멍하니 고개를 끄덕이는 엄마.
264|
265|그리고.
266|
267|“증거.”
268|
269|“…….”
270|
271|그래, 넌 기대도 안 했다. 나는 한숨과 함께 지갑을 던져 주었다.
272|
273|“뭐야?”
274|
275|“확인해 봐.”
276|
277|하연이가 의구심 가득한 눈으로 나를 바라보다가 지갑을 뒤지기 시작한다. 워낙 든 게 없는 지갑이라 ‘그것’을 찾는 데에는 얼마 걸리지 않았다.
278|
279|“헐.”
280|
281|손에 들린 카드 한 장. 이틀 전 협회에서 발급받은 C급 헌터 자격증이다.
282|
283|“위조된 거 아냐?”
284|
285|“맞을래?”
286|
287|“진짠가 보네.”
288|
289|“그거 위조하면 중범죄야, 인마.”
290|
291|“저 돈은? 오빠 말대로 그, 최 팀장인가 뭔가 하는 그 사람이 준 거야?”
292|
293|“몇 번 말해야 믿을래.”
294|
295|“350번 정도?”
296|
297|말과는 달리 이제는 믿는 눈치다. 은색으로 반짝이는 C급 헌터 자격증, 차곡차곡 쌓은 3억 원의 돈다발.
298|
299|전부 이 낡고 좁은 거실과는 동 떨어진 물건들이다.
300|
301|멍한 눈으로 앉아 있던 엄마가 신음처럼 중얼거렸다.
302|
303|“이게 다 무슨 일이라니…….”
304|
305|하연이도 세상 다 산 노인네처럼 허허 웃는다.
306|
307|“그러게. 살다 보니 별일이 다 있네.”
308|
309|“너 아직 스무 살도 안 됐거든.”
310|
311|“말이 그렇다는 거지. 근데 엄마.”
312|
313|“으, 응?”
314|
315|“탄내 나.”
316|
317|“맞다, 찌개!”
318|
319|반쯤 풀려 있던 엄마의 눈이 번쩍 뜨인다. 급한 대로 내가 몸을 일으켰지만, 부엌은 이미 초토화가 되어 있었다.
320|
321|뒤이어 따라온 엄마가 발을 동동 굴렀다.
322|
323|“아이고, 이걸 어째!”
324|
325|잔뜩 졸아 버린 국물에 숯덩이가 된 생선. 오랜만에 집밥을 먹을 수 있을 것 같아 기대했는데…….
326|
327|뭐, 이런 전개도 나쁘지 않지.
328|
329|“오랜만에 외식이나 하러 가요.”
330|
331|평소 같았으면 식당 가격의 부조리를 일장연설 했을 엄마도, 치킨이나 시켜 달라고 했을 하연이도 이번만큼은 조용했다.
332|
333|“동생아.”
334|
335|“네, 오라버니.”
336|
337|“돈 챙겨라.”
338|
339|“옛썰.”
340|
341|하연이가 기다렸다는 듯이 돈다발을 쓸어 담았다.
342|
343|
344|
345|* * *
346|
347|
348|
349|“손님. 죄송하지만 저희 레스토랑은 복장 규정이…….”
350|
351|코스 요리 먹는 데 1인당 수십만 원을 지불해야 한다는 고급 레스토랑의 지배인이 난처한 웃음을 지었다.
352|
353|“복장 규정이요?”
354|
355|“네. 보시면 아시겠지만 다른 손님들도 마찬가지거든요.”
356|
357|진짜네. 남자고 여자고 할 것 없이 죄다 정장에 원피스, 심지어는 드레스도 있다.
358|
359|‘시바, 누가 보면 무도회장에 춤추러 온 줄 알겠네.’
360|
361|여기가 무슨 18세기 프랑스야?
362|
363|국밥집만 드나들었던 내게는 엄청난 문화 충격이다.
364|
365|“그냥 다른 데 가자.”
366|
367|“그래, 하연이가 이 근처 맛집 많이 알더라.”
368|
369|나보다도 식구들이 더 무안해하는 것 같아 그냥 나왔다.
370|
371|레스토랑 유리에 우리 셋의 모습이 비친다. 오랜만의 외식이라고 신경 써서 입었을 게 분명한데, 가진 옷이라고는 죄다 시장 메이커에 오래 입은 티가 난다.
372|
373|‘돈이 부족했나?’
374|
375|나 먹는 거, 입는 거 아껴 가며 번 돈의 대부분을 집에 보냈다.
376|
377|F급 헌터였을 때도 남들보다 배로 일하니 결코 적은 돈은 아니었을 텐데.
378|
379|“아들, 삼겹살 먹으러 갈까? 아침부터 기름진 음식은 좀 그런가?”
380|
381|“삼겹살 좋지. 엄마가 뭘 좀 아네. 친구가 저 앞 사거리 고기집 갔는데 엄청 맛있었대.”
382|

“I-I’ll turn off up ahead.”

[P26]
The young man hugged the drink box tight until the blue truck disappeared from view, as if someone might snatch it away.

[P27]
“Sniff. Sniff.”

[P28]
Of course, he didn’t forget to smell it every chance he got.

[P29]
*This guy’s completely insane.*

[P30]
The AC was blasting inside the car, but Mr. Kim’s back was soaked with cold sweat. And this was his first fare of the day.

[P31]
What a thoroughly cursed day.

[P33]
Vroom.

[P34]
The moment I handed over the fare and shut the door, the taxi shot off like a bullet.

[P35]
Anyone watching would’ve thought a monster was chasing him. What if he got into an accident?

[P36]
I clicked my tongue and headed into the apartment complex, still cradling yesterday’s drink box against my chest.

[P37]
*Three hundred million won.*

[P38]
That was about as much as I’d saved over three full years as an F-rank Hunter. Of course, I didn’t have a single won of it left now.

[P39]
*I spent it all paying off debts.*

[P40]
There had been a time when I was drowning in debt, but I’d gritted my teeth and kept going until things gradually got better. I’d even moved my family into a safe-zone apartment near Ilsan.

[P41]
Lately, though, my life had been like a roller coaster.

[P42]
A roller coaster that would plummet if the System disappeared…

[P43]
No. I was home for the first time in months. I needed to stop thinking about that.

[P44]
*Which building and unit was it again?*

[P45]
I only came by once every couple of months, so this always happened.

[P46]
I glared at the tightly packed apartment buildings, then pulled out my phone and called. It rang for quite a while before the line finally connected.

[P47]
Click.

[P48]
“Hello?”

[P49]
I’d expected Hayeon to still be asleep this early, but her voice was perfectly clear.

[P50]
“You were already up?”

[P51]
“Of course I’m up. Do you know what time it is?”

[P52]
“It’s not even seven.”

[P53]
“I study better when I wake up early.”

[P54]
My little sister never failed to impress me. Jinho, who considered waking up in the morning one of the seven deadly sins, should’ve heard that.

[P55]
“Why’d you call?”

[P56]
“I’m out front.”

[P57]
“Huh? Out front?”

[P58]
“Yeah. But I forgot which one is ours.”

[P59]
“……Again? You really are something. Wait there.”

[P60]

[P61]
Even from a distance, she radiated the aura of a total bum. The look on her face said that everything in the world was too much trouble, and I couldn’t help laughing.

[P62]
“Jin Hayeon!”

[P63]
“Don’t yell. You’ll wake people up.”

[P64]
……Yeah. That was my little sister.

[P65]
“What brings you here? You didn’t even tell us you were coming.”

[P66]
“Do I have to announce it before coming to my own house?”

[P67]
“You show up so rarely. The residents’ association president probably visits more often than you do.”

[P68]
“That bad?”

[P69]
“That bad.”

[P70]
The elevator stopped. Hayeon punched in the code at the front door and turned the handle.

[P71]
And there—

[P72]
“Son!”

[P73]
Someone stood beaming at me.

[P74]
Wrinkled hands. A perm half fallen out. She looked as delighted as a child receiving a surprise gift.

[P75]
My throat tightened. I scratched my chin, then broke into a helpless smile.

[P76]
“I’m home, Mom.”

[P77]
I had finally come back.

[P78]
To the place where my family was waiting.

[P79]
Home.

[P81]
Sizzle, sizzle.

[P82]
Mom was busy making breakfast in the kitchen. A delicious smell drifted through the air.

[P83]
“Look at Lady Kim, all excited because her son’s finally home.”

[P84]
Hayeon scratched her stomach and plopped down beside me.

[P85]
The old sofa sagged beneath her.

[P86]
What a pig.

[P87]
“Is she making a lot?”

[P88]
“Yeah. A whole feast. Looks like we’re eating well today.”

[P89]
She answered without taking her eyes off her phone.

[P90]
“You haven’t seen your brother in ages. Aren’t you happy to see me?”

[P91]
“Huh?”

[P92]
“I mean, you could at least massage my shoulders after everything I’ve been through.”

[P93]
Hayeon let out a long sigh.

[P94]
“What’s gotten into you, Mr. Taekyung? We don’t have that kind of relationship.”

[P95]
“……Listen to that attitude.”

[P96]
We’d been bickering like this forever, but I still felt a little hurt.

[P97]
I mean, I’d barely made it home after nearly dying!

[P98]
“That got to you just now, didn’t it?”

[P99]
Her instincts were terrifying.

[P100]
“Go get ready for school, you school-lunch brat.”

[P101]
“Mm. Today’s the school anniversary.”

[P102]
My fist trembled.

[P103]
I wanted to smack the back of her irritating head right then and there, but if I did, I’d really lose.

[P104]
“You want to hit me, don’t you? Your fist is shaking.”

[P105]
“You’re lucky you’re a girl. If you had balls, I would’ve—”

[P106]
“Mom! Oppa’s sexually harassing me!”

[P107]
“Hey, hey!”

[P108]
“He said my b—mmph!”

[P109]
I clamped a hand over Hayeon’s mouth. She thrashed, hitting and pinching me, but she was still just a nineteen-year-old girl. It didn’t hurt.

[P110]
Then one of her flailing feet accidentally slammed into the drink box I’d carefully set in the corner of the sofa.

[P111]
Thump.

[P112]
Flutter.

[P113]
The box sprang wide open.

[P114]
Yellow bundles of bills spilled across the living-room floor.

[P115]
Hayeon froze.

[P116]
“Come on, stop fighting and eat your breakf—”

[P117]
Mom had come out of the kitchen too.

[P118]
Everything in the living room stopped as if someone had hit pause. Only the quiet simmering of the stew filled the silence.

[P119]
Sizzle, sizzle.

[P120]
I smiled awkwardly.

[P121]
“Can’t we talk about this after breakfast?”

[P122]
“……Son?”

[P123]
“Mmph, mmph.”

[P124]
It looked like breakfast would be delayed for quite a while.

[P126]
I told my family a suitably edited version of everything that had happened.

[P127]
My reawakening as a C-rank Hunter, and where the money had come from.

[P128]
“So that’s what happened.”

[P129]
Their reactions fell into two categories.

[P130]
“I see.”

[P131]
Mom nodded blankly.

[P132]
And then—

[P133]
“Proof.”

[P134]
“……”

[P135]
Yeah. I hadn’t expected anything else from you.

[P136]
I sighed and tossed Hayeon my wallet.

[P137]
“What’s this?”

[P138]
“Take a look.”

[P139]
She eyed me suspiciously, then started rummaging through it. There was barely anything inside, so it didn’t take her long to find *it*.

[P140]
“Whoa.”

[P141]
She held up a single card.

[P142]
It was the C-rank Hunter license the Association had issued me two days ago.

[P143]
“This isn’t fake, is it?”

[P144]
“Want to get hit?”

[P145]
“Guess it’s real.”

[P146]
“Forging one is a serious crime, you idiot.”

[P147]
“What about the money? Did that Team Leader Choi or whatever his name is really give it to you, like you said?”

[P148]
“How many times do I have to tell you before you believe me?”

[P149]
“About three hundred and fifty?”

[P150]
Despite what she said, she seemed to believe me now.

[P151]
A silver C-rank Hunter license. Three hundred million won in neatly stacked bundles.

[P152]
Every bit of it looked completely out of place in this old, cramped living room.

[P153]
Mom sat staring blankly before murmuring as if in a daze.

[P154]
“What on earth is happening…?”

[P155]
Hayeon chuckled like an old woman who had seen everything life had to offer.

[P156]
“I know. Live long enough and you see everything.”

[P157]
“You’re not even twenty.”

[P158]
“It’s just an expression. But, Mom.”

[P159]
“Y-Yes?”

[P160]
“I smell something burning.”

[P161]
“Oh, right! The stew!”

[P162]
Mom’s half-lidded eyes flew open. I hurried to my feet, but the kitchen was already a disaster zone.

[P163]
Mom rushed in after me, stamping her feet.

[P164]
“Oh no! What do we do?”

[P165]
The broth had boiled down to almost nothing, and the fish had turned into lumps of charcoal. I’d been looking forward to a home-cooked meal after so long, but…

[P166]
Well, this wasn’t such a bad turn of events either.

[P167]
“Let’s go out to eat. It’s been a while.”

[P168]
Normally, Mom would’ve launched into a long speech about the absurd price of restaurant food, while Hayeon would’ve asked us to order fried chicken instead. This time, they both stayed quiet.

[P169]
“Little sister.”

[P170]
“Yes, dear brother.”

[P171]
“Grab the money.”

[P172]
“Yessir.”

[P173]
As if she’d been waiting for the order, Hayeon swept up the bundles of cash.

[P174]
* * *

[P175]
“I’m sorry, but our restaurant has a dress code…”

[P176]
The manager of the upscale restaurant—where a course meal cost several hundred thousand won per person—gave us an awkward smile.

[P177]
“A dress code?”

[P178]
“Yes. As you can see, all our other guests are dressed accordingly.”

[P179]
He was right. Men and women alike wore suits and dresses. Some were even in evening gowns.

[P180]
*Shit. Anyone watching would think they’d come to dance at a ball.*

[P181]
What was this, eighteenth-century France?

[P182]
For someone like me, who’d only ever gone to gukbap[^1] places, it was a massive culture shock.

[P183]
“Let’s just go somewhere else.”

[P184]
“Yeah. Hayeon knows a lot of good restaurants around here.”

[P185]
My family seemed even more embarrassed than I was, so I simply walked out.

[P186]
The restaurant windows reflected the three of us. They had clearly put care into dressing up for our first meal out in a long time, but everything they owned was cheap market-brand clothing, visibly worn with age.

[P187]
*Had they been that short on money?*

[P188]
I’d sent most of what I earned home while cutting back on my own food and clothes.

[P189]
Even when I was an F-rank Hunter, I’d worked twice as hard as everyone else. It couldn’t have been a small amount.

[P190]
“Son, should we go get pork belly? Maybe something greasy is a bit much this early in the morning.”

[P191]
“Pork belly sounds good. Mom knows what’s what. A friend of mine went to the barbecue place at the intersection up ahead and said it was amazing.”

[P192]
Just pork belly.

[P193]
I had a C-rank Hunter license in my wallet and a bag stuffed with cash. They knew that. They could afford to splurge without worrying.

[P194]
*That’s why I work.*

[P195]
Someone once said money couldn’t buy happiness. That happiness didn’t come with a price tag.

[P196]
Personally, I had one thing to say to people who spouted that crap.

[P197]
*Fuck off.*

[P198]
You can’t spend money when you don’t have any.

[P199]
After spending all night wondering what to do with it, I’d finally made up my mind.

[P200]
For today, at least, I would spare no expense on my family.

[P201]
And now, that resolve swelled even stronger.

[P202]
“Let’s eat a little later.”

[P203]
Without waiting for an answer, I flagged down a passing taxi.

[P204]
“Where to?”

[P205]
“Mirae Department Store.”

[P206]
It was supposedly the biggest and most expensive department store in the area. In the rearview mirror, Mom’s eyes widened.

[P207]
“The department store?”

[P208]
Meanwhile, the corners of Hayeon’s mouth curled up slyly.

[P209]
“Nice. My rich oppa can buy me clothes too.”

[P210]
Sharp as ever. She caught on immediately.

[P211]
I gave a short laugh.

[P212]
“Buy whatever you want.”

[P213]
“Really?”

[P214]
“Pick out Mom’s things first.”

[P215]
“Okay.”

[P216]
“You’ve raised a devoted son, ma’am. Ha ha.”

[P217]
Only then did Mom smile at the driver’s banter.

[P218]
* * *

[P219]
“You’re really buying everything?”

[P220]
“Everything.”

[P221]
Once I confirmed it one last time, Hayeon tore through the department store like a colt off its reins. She scanned the clothes with a terrifyingly keen eye and moved so fast I started to wonder if she was an Awakened.

[P222]
At first, Mom looked at the price tags more than the clothes. Before long, though, she started joining in enthusiastically.

[P223]
“Mom, what do you think of this?”

[P224]
“Isn’t it too short?”

[P225]
“This one!”

[P226]
“That’s nice.”

[P227]
“This too!”

[P228]
“That’s pretty. Excuse me, miss—do you have this one size larger?”

[P229]
Two hours later, I began to feel a change in my body.

[P230]
*I’m dying.*

[P231]
For reasons I couldn’t explain, I was suffering from extreme shortness of breath and agonizing pain in my legs.

[P232]
A sense of helplessness comparable to what I’d felt facing Jopil in Murim engulfed my entire body.

[P233]
“Oppa, how do I look?”

[P234]
“Ugly. Get lost.”

[P235]
“Son, try this on.”

[P236]
“I don’t think I need to. I’ll take it.”

[P237]
I have no idea how many clothes we bought that day or how much we spent.

[P238]
All I know is that by the time we finished shopping, one of the department store’s top executives came to see us off.

[P239]
“Welcome.”

[P240]
The manager of the restaurant with the strict dress code didn’t even recognize us.

[P241]
“Wow, I’ve never eaten anything like this before.”

[P242]
“I know. How do they make the food look so pretty?”

[P243]
Mom and Hayeon whispered to each other, their cheeks flushed.

[P244]
We’d spent dozens of times more than the several-hundred-thousand-won course meal just so we could eat it, but not a single won felt wasted that day.

[P245]
“But I want rice. This is too rich.”

[P246]
“Why are the portions so small?”

[P247]
……I pretended not a single won felt wasted.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. - Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. - a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 52

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃52화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|오전 여섯 시.
  6|
  7|택시 기사 김 씨는 오늘의 첫 손님을 태웠다. 그리고 10분 만에 후회했다.
  8|
  9|‘재수 옴 붙었네.’
 10|
 11|겉보기로는 멀쩡하게 생긴 청년이다. 근육질의 듬직한 덩치에 얼굴은 멀끔해서 많이 쳐 줘야 20대 중후반으로 보였다.
 12|
 13|그런데…….
 14|
 15|“킁카킁카.”
 16|
 17|이상하다. 좀 많이.
 18|
 19|“흐어어.”
 20|
 21|웬 드링크 박스를 보물처럼 꼭 껴안고, 30초에 한 번씩 슬쩍 열어 냄새를 맡는다. 그리고 뭐에 홀린 것처럼 몸을 부르르 떤다.
 22|
 23|‘시방 저게 뭐 하는 짓이여.’
 24|
 25|김 씨는 뒷골이 싸했다. 10년 넘게 택시를 몰았지만 이런 종류의 진상은 처음이다.
 26|
 27|그가 계속해서 옆자리 청년을 곁눈질하던 그 순간.
 28|
 29|“아저씨.”
 30|
 31|“예, 예?!”
 32|
 33|심장 떨어질 뻔했다.
 34|
 35|방금 전까지만 해도 퀭하던 청년의 눈동자가, 야수처럼 번뜩이고 있었다.
 36|
 37|“뒤에 트럭이요.”
 38|
 39|“트, 트럭이요? 파란색?”
 40|
 41|“네. 아까 사거리에서부터 따라오는 것 같지 않아요?”
 42|
 43|“예? 아니 뭐, 그렇긴 한 것 같은데.”
 44|
 45|“미행일지도 모르잖아요.”
 46|
 47|이건 또 무슨 참신한 개소린가.
 48|
 49|김 씨는 눈동자를 뒤룩뒤룩 굴리다가 결국 그가 원하는 듯해 보이는 원하는 대답을 내놨다.
 50|
 51|“여, 옆쪽으로 빠지겠습니다.”
 52|
 53|청년은 파란 트럭이 시야에서 사라질 때까지 드링크 박스를 꼭 껴안고 있었다. 마치 누군가가 뺏어 가기라도 할 것처럼.
 54|
 55|“습하. 습하.”
 56|
 57|물론 틈틈이 냄새를 맡는 것도 빼놓지 않았다.
 58|
 59|‘이건 제대로 미친놈이다.’
 60|
 61|차 내부는 에어컨 바람이 쌩쌩 부는데, 김 씨의 등허리는 식은땀으로 축축했다. 첫 개시부터 이 모양이라니.
 62|
 63|아주 재수 옴 붙은 날이다.
 64|
 65|
 66|
 67|* * *
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|부아앙.
 72|
 73|요금을 건네고 문을 닫자마자 택시가 총알처럼 튀어 나간다.
 74|
 75|누가 보면 뒤에서 몬스터라도 쫓아오는 줄 알겠네. 사고라도 나면 어쩌려고. 나는 쯧쯧 혀를 차고 아파트 단지로 들어섰다.
 76|
 77|품에는 어제 받은 드링크 박스를 소중히 껴안은 채였다.
 78|
 79|‘3억.’
 80|
 81|내가 F급 헌터 시절부터 꼬박 3년을 일해서 모은 돈이랑 비슷한 액수다. 물론 지금은 한 푼도 안 남았다.
 82|
 83|‘빚 갚는 데 다 썼지.’
 84|
 85|그렇게 빚에 허덕이던 때가 있었는데, 이 악물고 하다 보니 점점 나아졌다. 가족을 일산 근처의 안전지대 아파트로 이사 보내기도 했고. 근래 들어서는 뭐, 인생이 롤러코스터 같다.
 86|
 87|시스템이 사라지면 추락하는 롤러코스터…….
 88|
 89|아니다. 몇 달 만에 오는 집인데 이런 생각은 집어치우자.
 90|
 91|‘그런데 몇 동 몇 호였지?’
 92|
 93|두어 달에 한 번 꼴로 오는 집이다 보니 늘 이렇다.
 94|
 95|나는 다닥다닥 붙어 있는 아파트 단지를 노려보다가 핸드폰을 꺼내 전화를 걸었다. 한참 신호음이 울린 뒤에야 연결됐다.
 96|
 97|딸칵.
 98|
 99|- 여보세요?
100|
101|아직 이른 시각이라 자고 있을 줄 알았는데, 하연이의 목소리는 또렷했다.
102|
103|“일어나 있었어?”
104|
105|- 일어나 있어야지. 시간이 몇 신데.
106|
107|“아직 일곱 시도 안 됐는데.”
108|
109|- 일찍 일어나야 공부가 잘돼.
110|
111|내 동생이지만 감탄스럽다. 오전 기상을 7대 죄악쯤으로 여기는 진호 형이 이걸 들었어야 했는데.
112|
113|- 왜 전화했어?
114|
115|“내가 지금 집 앞이거든.”
116|
117|- 응? 집 앞이라고?
118|
119|“어. 근데 우리 집이 어딘지 까먹었어.”
120|
121|- ……또? 가지가지 한다, 진짜. 기다려.
122|
123|끊긴 전화를 붙잡고 몇 분쯤 기다렸을까, 어느 동 입구에서 여자애 하나가 슬리퍼를 질질 끌며 나타났다.
124|
125|멀리서도 느껴지는 날백수 포스. 세상 귀찮다는 그 표정을 보자 나도 모르게 웃음이 나왔다.
126|
127|“진하연!”
128|
129|“소리 지르지 마. 사람들 깨.”
130|
131|……그래, 이래야 내 동생이지.
132|
133|“웬일이야? 말도 없이.”
134|
135|“내가 우리 집 오는데 말하고 와야 되냐?”
136|
137|“하도 드문드문 오니까 그렇지. 부녀회장이 오빠보다 우리 집 더 자주 올걸?”
138|
139|“그 정도냐?”
140|
141|“그 정도지.”
142|
143|그때 엘리베이터가 멈췄다. 현관문 앞에 선 하연이가 비밀번호를 입력하고 문고리를 돌린다.
144|
145|그리고 그곳에…….
146|
147|“아들!”
148|
149|환하게 웃고 있는 한 사람이 있다. 주름진 손과 반쯤 풀린 파마머리. 깜짝 선물을 받은 어린아이처럼 좋아하는 그 모습.
150|
151|순간 목이 막힌 나는 턱을 긁적이다가 풀썩 웃어 버렸다.
152|
153|“저 왔어요, 엄마.”
154|
155|드디어 돌아왔다.
156|
157|가족이 기다리고 있는 그곳. 집으로.
158|
159|
160|
161|* * *
162|
163|
164|
165|지글지글.
166|
167|엄마는 부엌에서 아침 준비로 한창이다. 기분 좋은 냄새가 코끝을 맴돌았다.
168|
169|“오랜만에 아들 왔다고 아주 신나셨네, 우리 김 여사.”
170|
171|하연이가 배를 벅벅 긁으며 옆자리에 주저앉았다.
172|
173|낡은 소파가 푹 꺼진다. 돼지 같은 년.
174|
175|“요리 많이 준비하고 계셔?”
176|
177|“어. 완전 진수성찬. 덕분에 잘 먹겠네.”
178|
179|대답은 하는데, 눈은 핸드폰 화면에 박혀 있다.
180|
181|“넌 오랜만에 오빠 봤는데 반갑지도 않냐?”
182|
183|“응?”
184|
185|“아니, 뭐. 고생했다고 어깨라도 좀 주물러 줄 수도 있고.”
186|
187|하연이가 한숨을 푹 내쉬었다.
188|
189|“왜 이래, 태경 씨. 우리 그런 사이 아니잖아.”
190|
191|“……말하는 싸가지 봐라.”
192|
193|이렇게 티격태격 하는 게 하루 이틀은 아니지만 괜히 섭섭하다.
194|
195|나는, 어? 그렇게 죽을 고비 넘겨 가면서 겨우 돌아왔는데!
196|
197|“지금 울컥했다. 울컥했지?”
198|
199|눈치 하나는 귀신이다.
200|
201|“학교 갈 준비나 해. 급식충아.”
202|
203|“응. 오늘 개교기념일.”
204|
205|주먹이 파르르 떨린다. 당장이라도 저 얄미운 뒤통수를 후려치고 싶지만 그러면 진짜 지는 거다.
206|
207|“때리고 싶죠? 주먹 부들부들 하죠?”
208|
209|“넌 여자라서 살았다. 불알만 달려 있었어도…….”
210|
211|“엄마! 오빠가 나 성추행해!”
212|
213|“야, 야!”
214|
215|“오빠가 나한테 불. 읍, 읍!”
216|
217|입을 틀어 막힌 하연이가 발버둥 친다. 때리고, 꼬집고. 그래 봤자 열아홉 살 여자애라 아프지도 않다.
218|
219|그러다가 우연히, 녀석이 내뻗은 발이 소파 한구석에 고이 모셔 둔 드링크 박스를 강타했다.
220|
221|퍽.
222|
223|촤르르륵.
224|
225|활짝 열린 박스. 거실 바닥에 쏟아지는 누런 지폐 뭉치.
226|
227|순간, 하연이의 몸이 굳었다.
228|
229|“이제 그만들 싸우고 아침 먹……어.”
230|
231|거기에 부엌에서 나온 엄마까지.
232|
233|일시 정지 버튼을 누른 것처럼 모든 게 멈춘 거실에, 찌개 끓는 소리만 잔잔하게 깔렸다.
234|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
